title: Water Cycle and Hydrology
text: The water cycle (hydrological cycle) describes the continuous movement of water through the environment. Evaporation from oceans, lakes, and rivers converts liquid water to vapor, which rises into the atmosphere. At altitude, vapor cools and condenses around dust particles to form clouds (condensation). Water falls as precipitation (rain, snow, hail). Some soaks into the ground (infiltration), replenishing groundwater aquifers; the rest flows as surface runoff into streams and rivers, eventually returning to the ocean. Transpiration from plants also contributes significant water vapor to the atmosphere. The water cycle is driven by solar energy and gravity, and it distributes heat around the planet.
